briefings.title: A conversation with Alan cofounder and CTO Charles Gorintin
briefings.tldr: Over its ten-year journey to becoming a health-tech leader with 1.2 million members and €800 million in ARR, Alan has leveraged radical transparency, early international expansion, and a transformative AI-first strategy to drive exponential productivity and build sovereign European technology.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Over its ten-year journey to becoming a health-tech leader with 1.2 million members and €800 million in ARR, Alan has leveraged radical transparency, early international expansion, and a transformative AI-first strategy to drive exponential productivity and build sovereign European technology.

## Alan’s Scaling Milestones and the French Tech Ecosystem

* **Rapid Growth Metrics:** Co-founder and CTO Charles Gorintin highlighted Alan’s scale after ten years of growth:
    * **Scale:** Serving 1.2 million members across 35,000 covered companies.
    * **Financials and Team:** Generating €800 million in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) with a team of 800 employees.
    * **Footprint:** Present in France, Belgium, Spain, and Canada.
* **The Investor Profile:** High-profile athlete Kylian Mbappé is an investor in Alan, serving as a fitting partner given that high-level athletes view health as their primary "work tool."
* **Ecosystem Evolution (2016 vs. 2024):** 
    * **Historically:** In 2016, France lacked "big brothers or sisters" in tech to model scaling, with only a few outliers like Criteo and BlaBlaCar.
    * **Present Day:** France has transitioned from having almost no ecosystem to fostering multi-billion-dollar companies featured on the Next40 and French Tech 120. 
    * **Sovereignty Goal:** While still trailing the scale of US and Chinese giants, establishing local champions is critical to recovering both geopolitical and economic sovereignty.

## Public Trust and Global Expansion Strategies

* **Winning State Contracts:** Alan recently secured major public contracts with the French Ministry of Ecology, Ministry of Finance, and the Prime Minister's services.
    * **Overcoming Skepticism:** Historically, governments avoided buying from startups due to a lack of trust. Alan bypassed the "nobody ever got fired for buying IBM" bias by ensuring flawless operational execution after winning.
* **International Expansion Philosophy:** Gorintin advises startups to expand internationally early, even at the risk of failing.
    * **Avoiding the Domestic Trap:** Many French companies over-index on digging deeper into the domestic market and fail to ever leave. Alan expanded to Belgium, Spain, and Canada to establish global foundations early, despite the high cost.
    * **The AI Advantage:** Because the human body is identical globally, clinical products translate well across borders. AI agents now allow Alan to customize regional user experiences far more cheaply and quickly than was possible five years ago.

## The AI Revolution: "Mo" and European Tech Sovereignty

* **The Medical Agent "Mo":** Developed in-house starting in 2023 under first engineer Antoine Lizee, Mo is Alan’s dedicated medical AI assistant.
    * **Clinical Approval:** Scientific testing showed that 80% of users prefer interacting with Mo immediately over waiting 30 minutes to speak to a human doctor. 
    * **High Quality:** Peer-reviewing doctors rated 95% of Mo's automated responses as "good" or "excellent."
* **The Birth of Mistral AI:** Gorintin (a non-operational co-founder of Mistral AI) explained that Mistral was founded in mid-2022 to break absolute reliance on US-based OpenAI.
* **Fostering a Local AI Value Chain:** European tech sovereignty requires the entire application layer to aggressively adopt AI agents. By integrating AI at the consumer level, European companies generate the commercial demand needed to fund local datacenters, compute power, and energy infrastructure.

## Re-Engineering Operations and Management for the AI Era

* **The Exponential Productivity Shift:** Gorintin shared that Alan's revenue per full-time employee (FTE) grew linearly for years, but turned strictly exponential post-2022 following their deep-tier AI integration.
* **Redistributing the Productivity Windfall:** Gorintin outlines four ways companies can deploy AI-driven productivity gains:
    * **Cost reduction** (often too short-sighted).
    * **Quantity increase** (expanding services to more countries).
    * **Quality enhancement** (giving healthcare professionals more time to look patients in the eyes).
    * **Employee return** (moving closer to shorter workweeks).
* **AI-Ready Corporate Practices:** Alan operates on organizational pillars established in 2016 that perfectly align with AI capabilities:
    * **Radical Transparency & Written Culture:** All corporate decisions are documented in writing. AI search agents now perform instant internal corporate "archaeology," allowing employees to understand the exact context of decisions made years prior.
    * **The "Chesterton's Fence" Solution:** Written history prevents the common corporate pitfall of keeping bad processes simply because "that is how it has always been done."
    * **The Shift to Tuning Agents:** Operational managers at Alan have transitioned from "doing the work" to "tuning and monitoring the AI agents" that execute the work.

> "Our revenue per full-time employee was increasing almost linearly for several years until 2022 when we did our AI transformation. Since 2022, this curve has become exponential. Each person is capable of creating far more value with AI agents than they ever could with classic software." — Charles Gorintin

> "For me, the next generation of entrepreneurs must be ambitious. We have been a bit too complacent in Europe for too long, which has led some toward declinism. ... We have a new technology with AI that allows us to take back control of our destiny." — Charles Gorintin

briefings.title: AI Devices Are Coming | Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon
briefings.tldr: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon predicts that 2026 will be the inflection point for "agentic AI," triggering a paradigm shift where personalized AI agents displace the smartphone as the sole center of digital life.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon predicts that 2026 will be the inflection point for "agentic AI," triggering a paradigm shift where personalized AI agents displace the smartphone as the sole center of digital life. This transition is driving massive demand for on-device processing, new wearable form factors like smart glasses, and next-generation chip architectures, even as the industry battles severe near-term memory shortages.

## The Paradigm Shift to Agentic AI and the "Compute Continue"
* **The Rise of the Agent:** Amon forecasts that 2026 will be the year AI agents scale globally. 
    * Major operating system (OS) vendors are expected to integrate orchestrators and agent "claws" directly into their systems by summer.
* **Agents as the New Apps:** Traditional applications are transitioning from human-facing interfaces into backend endpoints that AI agents navigate on behalf of the user.
    * **Bespoke Functionality:** For example, instead of manually navigating a banking app, users will instruct an agent to retrieve transactions, plot custom charts, or dynamically pay a bill via a QR code.
* **The "Compute Continue":** The binary debate of "cloud versus edge" processing is obsolete. Computing is evolving into an integrated hybrid system where edge devices handle low-latency, real-time responses while seamlessly coordinating with cloud-level models.
* **Model Context Protocol (MCP):** This open-source protocol is essential to the agentic era, allowing AI assistants to connect and communicate dynamically across different applications, databases, and cloud services.

## The Evolving Landscape of Personal AI Hardware
* **A New Center of Gravity:** The smartphone will no longer be the absolute center around which wearables orbit. Instead, a user's chosen AI agent will become the center of their digital life, with phones, glasses, and other devices acting as peripheral endpoints.
* **The Dominance of Smart Glasses:** Amon identifies smart glasses as the most natural form factor for multimodal AI because they position cameras, microphones, and speakers directly close to human senses.
    * **Market Scaling:** Industry shipments of smart glasses are currently in the "multiple tens of millions" annually, with a clear trajectory to scale to hundreds of millions in a couple of years.
    * **Technological Roadmap:** Future smart glasses will advance beyond simple cameras and audio to incorporate projection displays, eye-tracking, and hand-gesture controls.
* **Alternative Form Factors:** Qualcomm is actively collaborating with AI and cloud partners on more than 40 distinct wearable designs, including jewelry, camera-enabled earbuds, watches, pendants, and pins. 
* **New Market Entrants:** Because agent-centric ecosystems are horizontal rather than vertical, the barrier to entry has lowered. This allows non-traditional consumer brands—such as fashion houses and AI startups like OpenAI (partnering with hardware designer Jony Ive)—to enter the consumer electronics space.

## Silicon Architecture Demands and the CPU Renaissance
* **The Efficiency Imperative:** Packaged AI workloads must run efficiently on wearable devices that cannot support liquid cooling or heavy batteries. This plays directly into Qualcomm's core mobile expertise of optimizing high-performance compute in thermally constrained environments.
* **The CPU Renaissance:** While Neural Processing Units (NPUs) and Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) are expanding on System-on-Chips (SOCs) to handle localized AI models, the central processing unit (CPU) is seeing a critical resurgence.
    * **Orchestration Workloads:** CPUs are highly critical because the sophisticated "orchestrator" software that manages agent tasks lives on the CPU.
    * **Data Center Expansion:** To capitalize on this, Qualcomm plans to announce its new CPU for data centers on June 24.

## Semiconductor Supply Chain and Memory Bottlenecks
* **Severe Memory Shortages:** The industry is grappling with post-pandemic style supply constraints. High-bandwidth memory chips are being heavily funneled to AI data centers, creating a severe bottleneck for consumer electronics.
* **Capacity Resolution Timeline:** While some industry experts predict supply constraints will persist until 2028, Amon is more optimistic, anticipating that new capacity and more efficient silicon architectures will become available in the second half of 2027.
* **A Structural Upgrade Cycle:** Amon emphasizes that the current demand spike is not a typical semiconductor cycle. Instead, it represents a structural, global upgrade of the world's computing infrastructure to support token generation and AI-native software.

## Notable Quotes

> "The phone is going to continue to be your phone... But the phone also's going to have those orchestrators... You're going to see between now and summer, every OS vendor talking about their OS having an orchestrator... agents are the new apps." — **Cristiano Amon**

> "In the future, and is a very near future, especially as agents start to get scale: the center of your digital experience is the agent that you choose... And now everything is around the agent. The phone is around the agent, the new classes of devices... are going to be around the agent as well." — **Cristiano Amon**

> "We have significantly more demand than supply. And memory has become a bottleneck... I think some time in '27 or at least the second half we should see more capacity becoming available, different architectures that are going to make use of memory more efficient." — **Cristiano Amon**

briefings.title: AP EXCLUSIVE: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says society needs 'new social norms' in age of AI
briefings.tldr: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang outlines a massive, multi-trillion-dollar transition to reinvent modern computing, emphasizing that the U.S. must pair world-class AI model development with domestic manufacturing, robust energy growth, and updated social norms to lead this new industrial revolution.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang outlines a massive, multi-trillion-dollar transition to reinvent modern computing, emphasizing that the U.S. must pair world-class AI model development with domestic manufacturing, robust energy growth, and updated social norms to lead this new industrial revolution.

---

## Reinventing Computing and the Next Era of AI
* **A 60-Year Paradigm Shift:** Jensen Huang states that the tech industry is reinventing the computer for the first time since the invention of the IBM System/360 in 1964. 
    * Computers are transitioning from pre-recorded, coded instructions to real-time problem-solving systems.
    * Over the next 10 years, tens of trillions of dollars in capital expenditure will be spent to replace the old global computing infrastructure.
* **Smarter, Truth-Grounded Models:** Future AI will be safer, have better guardrails, and be grounded in deeper truth.
    * Rather than "guessing" answers, next-generation AI will actively research, evaluate multiple sources of information, and analyze truthfulness before delivering results.

## Re-industrialization and Silicon Photonics in Texas
* **Strategic Coherent-Nvidia Partnership:** Nvidia is partnering with Coherent at their Sherman, Texas facility, utilizing a $50 million federal CHIPS Act award to strengthen the domestic AI supply chain.
    * The partnership will quadruple the output of the Sherman facility in just one year to meet the massive demand for accelerated computing.
* **The Role of Silicon Photonics:** The Sherman plant manufactures world-leading 6-inch indium phosphide lasers.
    * These lasers convert electrical signals to light (silicon photonics), allowing chips separated by hundreds or thousands of feet inside an AI factory to connect and work seamlessly as a single supercomputer.
* **U.S. Manufacturing Revival:** The rapid build-out of AI data centers, chip fabs, and packaging plants has already created approximately 600,000 jobs in the U.S. 
    * Huang emphasizes that this shift brings back high-paying manufacturing jobs for "builders and makers," balancing an economy previously dominated by information workers.

## The Five Layers of AI and the Energy Deficit
* **The AI Stack:** Huang outlines the five foundational layers of AI: Energy, Chips, Infrastructure, Models, and Applications.
* **The U.S. Energy Bottleneck:** While the U.S. is world-class in chips, infrastructure, and models, it is "woefully behind" in energy production.
    * **Energy Imperative:** Huang argues that AI data centers present a once-in-a-generation opportunity to use market forces—completely free of government subsidies—to fund sustainable energy, nuclear power, and grid upgrades. Without pro-energy growth, the U.S. cannot sustain its AI infrastructure.
* **The Application Layer:** U.S. society must overcome its hesitation to adopt AI at the top application layer (e.g., healthcare, manufacturing, and transport) to avoid being left behind by international competitors.

## Geopolitics, Export Controls, and Taiwan's Ecosystem
* **Balancing National Security and Economic Prosperity:** While national security must be a top priority, Huang warns against "over-exercising" export controls, which could have unintended consequences for U.S. economic leadership.
    * **The China Market:** Huang stresses that the U.S. should continue to export previous-generation hardware to compete in China, noting that completely ceding the massive Chinese market would only force regional competitors to scale and grow into global giants.
* **Taiwan as a Critical Partner:** Taiwan remains the global epicenter of the chip supply chain.
    * Beyond manufacturing chips, Taiwanese tech giants (such as TSMC, Foxconn, and Wistron) are strategic partners actively helping the U.S. establish domestic fabs and assembly plants in states like Arizona.

## Adapting to AI: Social Norms and Public Engagement
* **The Need for New Social Norms:** Huang compares the anxiety surrounding AI to the early days of automobiles, when society had to develop new social norms, sidewalks, crosswalks, and seatbelts to safely integrate cars.
    * "We have to deal with regulation, technology, and social norms at the same time."
* **Lowering the Tech Divide:** AI is the most accessible technology in history because users do not need to learn coding to use it; they can simply talk to it.
* **Active Public Engagement:** Huang urges the public, including workers concerned about job displacement, to directly try free AI tools like ChatGPT to explore how it can assist them in their existing careers.
* **Skepticism Toward Government Ownership:** Addressing floated proposals regarding government ownership stakes in AI companies, Huang questioned the necessity, pointing out that Americans already naturally benefit from these domestic companies through tax revenues, jobs, and investment portfolios.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "We're reinventing the computer for the first time in 60 years... You no longer have to code, and no longer record information in advance... It is able to now solve problems in real time." 
> — **Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO**

> "When automobiles came, we needed to create new social norms... We have sidewalks, we have crosswalks, we have jaywalking discouraged. All of that combination of social norms, regulations, safer cars, seatbelts... it's all of it at the same time [for AI]." 
> — **Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO**

> "It is a false choice to have... we can have national security, that is absolutely foremost, we want our technology industry to succeed around the world, and in order to do that, you have to compete." 
> — **Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO**

briefings.title: Clay’s Unusual Path to Building a Multi-Billion Dollar Company
briefings.tldr: Kareem Amin, co-founder and CEO of Clay, outlines his unconventional philosophy of building a highly successful software company by creating from a place of "wholeness" rather than "lack," optimizing for self-respect, and embracing true risk.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Kareem Amin, co-founder and CEO of Clay, outlines his unconventional philosophy of building a highly successful software company by creating from a place of "wholeness" rather than "lack," optimizing for self-respect, and embracing true risk. By viewing go-to-market tools as an open-ended programming medium rather than static software, Clay scaled from 1 to 100 in two years, utilizing operational and product insights drawn from non-dual meditation, music theory, and magic.

---

## The Origin and Strategy of Clay: "Go-To-Market Engineering"

* **The Vision of Democratized Programming:** Co-founders Kareem Amin and Nicola started Clay to give the power of computation to non-technical business users. They aimed to establish a highly fluid, low-latency interaction between humans and machines, heavily inspired by music software like Ableton Live and Douglas Engelbart's 1968 "Mother of All Demos."
* **Targeting Sales and Marketing:** In 2017, they selected go-to-market (GTM) teams because sales and marketing personnel are highly creative but lack the engineering resources to execute complex data experiments at scale.
    * *Example:* A garbage-disposal company using Google Satellite View to identify locations with high trash accumulation to target sales outreach—an innovative idea easily automated via Clay's flexible platform.
* **The Three Core Growth Pillars:** Clay’s rapid growth from 1 to 100 in two years was enabled by three non-obvious foundational assumptions:
    * **Creative, Open-Ended Tools:** Rejecting the industry norm of simple, "coin-operated" sales software, Clay built a powerful, open-ended platform designed to let users discover unique "go-to-market alpha."
    * **Defining the "RevOps" Persona:** They positioned their tool for Revenue Operations (RevOps) and framed the discipline as "go-to-market engineering."
    * **Usage-Based Pricing:** They chose to bill based on platform usage rather than seat counts, ensuring that client productivity gains remained aligned with Clay's economic incentives.
* **The "Guitar" Analogy:** Amin contrast commoditized software with expressive software.
    * *Microwave vs. Guitar:* Most SaaS products are "microwaves" (commodity appliances with push-button utility). Clay is a "guitar"—a tool with simple, fixed parameters (six strings, 12 frets) that users can spend a lifetime mastering to create entirely unique outcomes.

---

## Redefining Risk, Courage, and "Post-Lack" Ambition

* **What Capitalism Truly Rewards:** Amin argues that capitalism rewards genuine risk-taking rather than hard work or pure talent. 
    * **The Formula for Real Risk:** True risk requires stepping into a situation where the outcome is genuinely unknown, paired with a high potential for personal, public shame. Amin warns that many founders avoid this by hedging and refusing to commit to a singular, specific customer group.
* **Creating from Wholeness vs. Lack:** VCs often search for founders with "a chip on their shoulder" who are motivated by an internal void. Amin consciously shifted to a "post-lack" state of mind.
    * *The Post-Lack Advantage:* Creating from a place of internal wholeness reduces corporate politics, minimizes organizational destructiveness, and serves as powerful negotiation leverage because the founder has nothing to lose.
* **Optimizing for Self-Respect:** Drawing parallels to Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky's experiences with the emptiness of massive wealth, Amin asserts that external prestige and adulation fail to satisfy. The only sustainable North Star is self-respect, which demands adhering to your own internal standards, which are inevitably higher than those of outside observers.

---

## The Three Elevators Statues: Courage, Justice, and Truth

Asked what abstract values he would build as statues in his office lobby, Amin highlighted three:

* **Courage:** Necessary to make decisive, scary commitments and follow them through to their logical, unhedged conclusions.
* **Justice (and Integrity):** Built on treating people with fairness and respect. Amin operates on being "long-term greedy," which requires absolute integrity so that partners, employees, and customers remain willing to build with you over decades.
* **Truth:** Inspired by a profound non-dual experience during a meditation retreat, Amin emphasizes the value of seeing reality as it is—recognizing that we are all deeply interconnected and that human suffering is shared. He views corporate and social squabbling as a tragic waste of human potential.

---

## Unconventional Management and Operations

* **Over-Investing in the Non-Obvious:** Clay deliberately over-allocates resources to areas most software companies under-fund, such as brand, content, community, and recruiting.
    * *PM-Level Content Compensation:* Clay hired an early employee, Mishthi, for a content role but compensated her on par with a Product Manager, reflecting their high valuation of brand communication.
* **Deep Commitment to High-Potential Talent:** Rejecting the "hire fast, fire fast" startup trope, Clay will support struggling employees for up to nine months to understand if the context, role, or management style is the limiting factor. This approach results in a 50% success rate in turning struggling employees into organizational superstars.
* **Radical Transparency in Terminations:** When letting people go, Amin believes in establishing a shared reality. He explicitly takes personal executive ownership of the decision rather than hiding behind performance metrics, and he promises departing employees that he will speak honestly but supportively to future reference-checkers.

---

## Cross-Disciplinary Inspiration: Magic, Clowning, and Music Theory

* **Magicians and "Re-Enchanting" the World:** Clay actively incorporates magicians into their events. Amin learns from magic's emphasis on storytelling and psychology to spark curiosity and wonder. In an era dominated by AI, Amin believes businesses must help "re-enchant" a world that people falsely assume they fully understand.
* **The Four Types of Clowning:** Amin studies clowning to expand his personal and organizational boundaries. He breaks down clowning into four practices:
    * *Physical:* Traditional slapstick.
    * *Emotional Range:* Navigating people rapidly through happiness and sadness.
    * *The Jester:* Speaking truth to power.
    * *The Trickster:* Delivering deep spiritual truths through humor.
* **Music Theory and "The Emancipation of Dissonance":** Drawing from music theory, Amin cites Arnold Schoenberg's concept of *The Emancipation of Dissonance*—the historical progression of music accepting increasingly complex, dissonant sounds as harmonious. Clay applies this by learning to accept unconventional ideas and non-traditional human behaviors as highly productive when placed in the right corporate context.

---

## Vision, Wealth, and the Corporate Lifecycle

* **The Fallacy of Constant Vision:** Amin argues that leaders do not always need a pre-packaged grand vision and should never manufacture one to satisfy public expectations. Instead, they should optimize for discovery, letting the vision emerge naturally.
* **The Purpose of Wealth:** Material abundance is primarily valuable because it buys back a founder’s time. Operating a company because you *choose* to, rather than because you *need* to, unlocks the freedom to take much larger, unhedged swings.
* **A "Death Doula" for Companies:** Amin challenges the societal assumption that every business must scale infinitely. He proposes that companies should have natural lifecycles. Once a company achieves its core mission (similar to Microsoft's original goal of placing a computer on every desk), it should be allowed to gracefully disband or birth new ventures rather than transforming into a low-quality, value-extracting "zombie" corporation.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "I think capitalism rewards risk more than anything else... To take real risk, you need to not know what's going to happen genuinely, and it needs to be coupled with a high potential for shame." — **Kareem Amin**

> "I had this moment where I was like, you know what, I'm not going to create from a place of lack anymore... I think you can create from a place of wholeness and in fact you will be less destructive in the world." — **Kareem Amin**

> "We’re not building a microwave... We’re building a guitar. With a guitar there's just six strings and 12 frets, but you could spend your whole life just getting better." — **Kareem Amin**

> "A death doula for companies is: if your company has achieved its mission, should we help it pass? ... Instead of trying to scale things that become zombies or become worse versions of their former selves." — **Kareem Amin**

briefings.title: Context Needed to Reach AGI, Says Databricks CEO
briefings.tldr: The primary bottleneck to achieving artificial general intelligence (AGI) in the enterprise is not raw intelligence, but a lack of organizational context.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
The primary bottleneck to achieving artificial general intelligence (AGI) in the enterprise is not raw intelligence, but a lack of organizational context. Databricks is addressing this constraint by building "agentic-first" database architectures and semantic ontologies that enable AI agents to compute complex business queries in real time.

## Context as the Bottleneck to AGI
* **The Context Gap:** While modern AI models possess immense intelligence, they are not yet widely integrated into enterprise workflows because they lack access to internal company data, processes, and institutional knowledge. 
* **Enterprise Ontology:** To solve this, Databricks is utilizing enterprise ontologies—interconnected webs of organizational data that map how documents, people, and processes relate. 
    * **The Search Metaphor:** Instead of an AI agent searching through separate systems one by one (similar to early web search), an ontology acts as a centralized index (like Google) that allows agents to tap into computed knowledge instantly.

## Computational Agents vs. Recitative Agents
* **Genie 1's Computing Power:** Unlike traditional AI assistants that merely find and recite existing documents, Genie 1 can compute live data and perform complex mathematical queries on the fly.
    * **Novo Nordisk Case Study:** The pharmaceutical giant uses Genie 1 to allow its scientists to quickly analyze and compute trial data for drug studies (such as Ozempic), reducing analysis time to a fraction of what it was.
* **Databases Built for Agents (Lake-tap & Lakebase):** Modern database architecture was designed for human speeds, which are too slow and costly for high-frequency AI agent requests.
    * **Unified Infrastructure:** Lake-tap (L-tap) and Lakebase unify standard transactional databases with analytical data warehouses into a single, high-speed system optimized for AI agents.
    * **Prada Case Study:** Luxury brand Prada stores its KPIs within Lakebase, enabling AI agents to instantly compute and deliver accurate business metrics to leadership.

## Hurdles to Enterprise AI Adoption
* **Security and Legal Friction:** Even though Databricks has a 15-year track record of enterprise trust, actual deployment of deep AI systems is throttled by rigorous security and legal department reviews.
* **Chatbot Stagnation:** Because of these internal compliance hurdles, most corporate AI adoption is currently limited to low-risk chatbot use cases. Implementing AI in high-stakes areas like financial reporting or drug development requires significantly more time.

## Funding and Databricks' IPO Strategy
* **Aggressive Product Expansion:** Databricks is aggressively moving into new verticals with "agentic-first" products, including *Customer Lake* (marketing tech) and *Lake Watch* (security operations).
* **Funding and Research Costs:** Addressing rumors of a new funding round valuing Databricks at up to $75 billion, Ghodsi noted that recruiting top AI researchers and expanding globally requires substantial capital.
* **Postponing the IPO:** Ghodsi stands by his assertion that 2024 is a "terrible year" to go public. Databricks plans to remain private until the market stabilizes and there is more predictability post-major tech IPOs.

## Notable Quotes
> "These AIs are plenty smart... But then, yet, we're not seeing them in the workplace. They're not everywhere... Why is that? They just don't have the context. If you could take all of the data, all the processes, everything that people are thinking and put them in the models, they could actually help us tremendously." — Ali Ghodsi

> "The big difference between Genie 1 is that Genie 1 computes, other agents recite... What other agents will do is that they recite. They will try to find: is there a document that has this answer?... But what if that answer does not exist in any document and you have to actually compute it live?" — Ali Ghodsi

> "I prefer for the company to go public when, you know, waters are a little bit more calm and there's a little bit more predictability. Uh, so, you know, I stand by what I said. I think for most other companies, uh you know, it's probably best to wait it out." — Ali Ghodsi

briefings.title: Data + AI Summit Keynote 2026 | Day 1
briefings.tldr: At the Data + AI Summit 2026, Databricks unveiled Genie 1, an enterprise-grounded AI coworker, alongside major data-layer unifications including Lakehouse RT, Lakebase Postgres, and LTAP—a storage-level technology that eliminates complex Change Data Capture (CDC) pipelines by natively transcoding operational data into open lakehouse formats.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
At the Data + AI Summit 2026, Databricks unveiled Genie 1, an enterprise-grounded AI coworker, alongside major data-layer unifications including Lakehouse RT, Lakebase Postgres, and LTAP—a storage-level technology that eliminates complex Change Data Capture (CDC) pipelines by natively transcoding operational data into open lakehouse formats.

---

## The Agentic Shift: Genie 1 and Genie Ontology

*   **Context Over Intelligence:** Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi emphasized that frontier AI models do not suffer from an intelligence problem, but rather a context problem. To drive autonomous work, AIs must be grounded in an organization's specific data, operational history, and security structures.
*   **Genie Ontology and OntoRank:** To address the cost and accuracy limitations of generic AI agents, Databricks introduced Genie Ontology.
    *   **Automated Context Graph:** Running in the background, it constructs a comprehensive knowledge graph spanning Databricks tables, Google Drive, SharePoint, email, and calendars.
    *   **The OntoRank Algorithm:** A proprietary, PageRank-style algorithm designed by the Databricks research team to assess the authority of various enterprise data assets, code snippets, and organizational relationships.
    *   **Proven Results:** Internal benchmarks show a 30% improvement in reasoning accuracy and a 50% reduction in query runtimes compared to standard coding agents.
*   **Genie 1 Launch:** Now generally available, Genie 1 is positioned as a data-smart AI coworker integrated natively with Teams, Slack, iOS, and Android. To accelerate adoption, Databricks is offering $10 per user/month in free token credits.
*   **Expanded Genie Family:**
    *   **Genie Agents:** Enables business users to quickly turn conversations or specific document folders into shared, custom agents (e.g., automated HR bots).
    *   **Genie Code:** A specialized coding agent optimized for data engineering, pipeline writing, and automated machine learning modeling.

## Breaking the OLTP/OLAP Barrier: Lakehouse RT, Lakebase, and LTAP

*   **The HTAP Problem Solved:** Historically, Hybrid Transactional/Analytical Processing (HTAP) failed due to engine complexity and storage compromises. Databricks introduced **LTAP (Lake Transactional Analytical Processing)** to unify these systems at the storage layer.
    *   **Transcoding at Storage:** Using idle CPU capacity on storage services, LTAP transcodes row-oriented transactional data into column-oriented formats (Delta/Iceberg) inside the data lake in real time, bypassing performance bottlenecks.
    *   **Eliminating CDC:** This architecture completely bypasses fragile Change Data Capture (CDC) pipelines. Operational tables updated in Lakebase instantly appear as column-oriented tables in the Lakehouse with no pipeline maintenance required.
*   **Lakebase (Serverless Postgres on the Lake):** A fully managed, decoupled operational database that stores data cheaply on the lake.
    *   **Sub-Second Provisioning:** Provisions instances and generates branches/clones in under 500 milliseconds, allowing agents to instantly create isolated testing environments.
    *   **Cross-Cloud Disaster Recovery:** Offers fully managed, cross-cloud replication (e.g., active replication from AWS US-West to Azure US-East) for instant failover during cloud outages.
*   **Lakehouse RT (Powered by the Reyden Engine):** A real-time analytical engine designed for strict sub-second SLAs.
    *   **Algorithmic Dispatching:** Utilizes machine learning models trained on trillions of historical queries to select the most efficient processing algorithm at runtime.
    *   **High-Throughput Performance:** Demonstrated executing 12,000 queries per second with a tail latency of only 37 milliseconds on standardized TPC-H benchmarks.

## Automating Data Pipelines: Lakeflow and Genie ZeroOps

*   **Lakeflow Ingest & Design Upgrades:**
    *   **Lakeflow Connect:** Expanded to include over 100 native enterprise connectors.
    *   **Zerobus Ingest:** A fully managed, Kafka-wire-compatible service that lands streaming data directly into the Lakehouse at up to 12 GB/s without generating fragmented small files.
    *   **Lakeflow Designer:** Generally available visual, no-code data preparation environment that compiles directly into open-source Spark Declarative Pipelines.
    *   **Spark Real-Time Mode (RTM):** An open-source streaming framework capable of running continuous pipelines with sub-10 millisecond latency.
*   **Genie ZeroOps (Autonomous Maintenance):** Recognizing that data engineers spend over 50% of their time on pipeline maintenance, Databricks launched Genie ZeroOps to act as an autopilot for data operations.
    *   **Data-Plane Residency:** Unlike external agents, ZeroOps lives directly inside the secure data plane, eliminating security risks while providing native access to metrics, logs, and lineage.
    *   **End-to-End Self-Healing:** The agent automatically trains table-specific ML models to detect anomalies, traces root causes using Unity Catalog lineage, builds safe fixes, and tests them in isolated shallow clones before prompting engineers for PR approvals.

## Enterprise Governance and Agent Control: Unity AI Gateway

*   **Taming Runaway AI Costs:** To control skyrocketing token consumption and govern autonomous agents, Databricks announced the **Unity AI Gateway**, integrated directly into Unity Catalog and MLflow.
    *   **Centralized Observability:** Provides a single pane of glass to track token spend, enforce safety guardrails, and audit outputs.
    *   **User-Level Budgets:** Allows administrators to set granular, rate-limited spend ceilings down to individual user groups and employees.
    *   **Token Flexibility:** Enables enterprises to apply their committed Databricks contract spend directly toward frontier model tokens (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini) across any cloud.
    *   **Model Context Protocol (MCP):** Authenticates and manages both internal and third-party MCP servers, providing single-sign-on access to agent skills.
*   **OpenSharing:** An open-source extension of Delta Sharing that allows cross-organizational sharing of both Delta/Iceberg datasets and active AI assets (agents, models, and skills).

## Strategic Acquisitions and Platform Expansions

*   **Panther Labs Acquisition:** Databricks announced an agreement to acquire Panther Labs, a Python-based security platform. Panther's technology will power **Lakewatch**, an agentic, cloud-scale SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) system that stores security telemetry cheaply in the open lakehouse and deploys agents to autonomously triage threats.
*   **CustomerLake:** A new agentic Customer Data Platform (CDP) built directly on top of the Lakehouse. It leverages LLMs for automated customer identity deduplication and introduces "Infinity Campaigns" to generate continuous, hyper-personalized consumer marketing.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "AI does not have an intelligence problem right now... The problem we have is that AGI is not really completely permeating our organizations. Inside of your companies, you don't have hundreds of agents working for you doing autonomous work."  
> — *Ali Ghodsi, CEO of Databricks*

> "With LTAP we can finally combine the separate continents of OLTP and analytics into a single giant continent... [It] is HTAP done right and accomplishes the goals of HTAP without actually having a single query engine for it."  
> — *Reynold Xin, Co-Founder of Databricks*

> "One thing we really stand for at OpenAI is keeping humans at the center... That means we have this opportunity to sort of leverage these systems in cases that we really want, but also have a lot of time to think about where do we want the humans to fundamentally remain."  
> — *Greg Brockman, President and Co-Founder of OpenAI*

briefings.title: How Machiavelli's Florence bargained with Cesare Borgia for survival – Ada Palmer
briefings.tldr: Far from being a self-serving cynic, Niccolò Machiavelli was an intense patriot who wrote The Prince in isolated exile as a bespoke, secret manual to help the Medici stabilize a chaotic Italy, prioritizing his country's survival over his own wealth, career, and safety.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
Far from being a self-serving cynic, Niccolò Machiavelli was an intense patriot who wrote *The Prince* in isolated exile as a bespoke, secret manual to help the Medici stabilize a chaotic Italy, prioritizing his country's survival over his own wealth, career, and safety.

---

## The Volatile Geopolitical Landscape of Renaissance Italy

*   **The Severed Thread of Continuity:** Ada Palmer explains that long-term continuous governments possess inherent legitimacy. Once a regime is overthrown, that continuity is broken, leading to rapid-fire successions of overthrows. In Machiavelli's lifetime, this thread was cut for the majority of Italian city-states, creating a highly volatile environment ripe for constant replacement.
*   **The Destabilizing Force of the Papacy:** The Papacy wielded massive military and temporal power, but lacked hereditary succession. 
    *   **The Ten-Year Cycle:** Because popes were elected (often by a coalition of the previous pope's enemies), every decade brought a completely unpredictable new monarch who dismantled his predecessor's legacy and overthrew local governments to install his own family.
    *   **The Medici Objective:** Machiavelli wanted the Medici family (who controlled both Florence and the Papacy at the time) to conquer a large enough territory to force the Papacy to negotiate, creating a regional buffer of stability.

---

## Cesare Borgia and the Anatomy of Ruthless Power

*   **Firsthand Obsession:** Machiavelli had a terrifying, front-row seat next to Cesare Borgia (known as Valentino). Borgia possessed such polarizing, supernatural charisma that contemporaries debated whether he was a savior or the literal Antichrist.
*   **The "Boon of Polyphemus":** As Borgia swept through Italy, Machiavelli realized Florence could not permanently bribe him. He advised Florence to abandon its 300-year alliance with Bologna, abjectly swear loyalty to Borgia, and help him conquer others. 
    *   This strategy aimed to buy time, earning the "promise of the conqueror: I like you, my guest, I'll eat you last."
*   **Fortune vs. Strategy:** Machiavelli argues Borgia did everything right—including the infamous massacre at Senigallia where he invited conspirators to a "reconciliation" dinner and slaughtered them. Borgia only fell because of pure bad luck (fortune): he and his father, Pope Alexander VI, fell terminally ill at the exact same moment.
*   **The Pragmatism of Deception:** Machiavelli asserts that lying is highly effective if backed by fear. 
    *   **Borgia vs. Savonarola:** When Borgia betrayed allies, his remaining partners fell into line out of fear of being next. Conversely, the religious demagogue Savonarola was charismatic but not scary; when he began flip-flopping on his policies, his power base collapsed.

---

## Patronage, Nepotism, and the Renaissance System of Justice

*   **Patronage as Social Glue:** In the Renaissance, patronage and nepotism were the fundamental glues of society. Trust was entirely familial.
    *   **The Demand for Nepotism:** When Pope Paul III appointed a highly competent external general to lead the papal armies instead of his own incompetent illegitimate son, the Roman populace rioted. They demanded nepotism because they believed only a son's fate was tied close enough to the Pope's to prevent military betrayal.
*   **The Spiritual Purpose of Justice:** Unlike the modern ideal of blind, proportional justice, Renaissance law codes prescribed death for almost every minor offense but rarely carried it out. 
    *   **The Role of the Patron:** A defendant's patron (acting as an earthly "patron saint") would intervene to secure a pardon or a light fine. The legal process was designed to make the sinner fear for their life before a terrifying judge (representing God) and then experience mercy, structurally preparing their soul for divine judgment.
*   **The Inquisition as the Birth of Copyright:** Before copyright law, authors like Machiavelli panicked when printers published copies of their books riddled with typos, as there was no legal recourse. The Inquisition inadvertently solved this by requiring pre-publication theological checks. In exchange for submission to censorship, the church granted printers a monopoly license, which became the historical ancestor of copyright.

---

## Machiavelli’s Exile and the Art of Hidden Originality

*   **The Sacrifice of Isolated Exile:** After being tortured and exiled to a barren hamlet by the Medici, Machiavelli refused prestigious offers from foreign courts. Instead, he chose to rot in the countryside to write *The Prince* as a secret, proprietary "nuclear secret" intended solely to help the Florentine government survive.
*   **Originality Disguised as Commentary:** In the Renaissance, original ideas were out of vogue; cultural prestige demanded that all insights derive from antiquity. 
    *   **The Trellis Analogy:** To bypass this restriction, scholars used commentaries on ancient texts as a "trellis" to grow their own original ideas. Machiavelli hid his most innovative political theories—including checks and balances, political parties, and the psychological utility of religion—within his *Discourses on Livy*.

---

## The Divergence of the "Machiavellian" Myth from the Man

*   **"Old Nick" vs. The Patriot:** History split Machiavelli into two figures: the fictionalized Shakespearean villain "Old Nick" (representing self-serving, atheistic malice) and the historical Niccolò (a selfless patriot who sacrificed his livelihood for Florence).
*   **Secular Statecraft in the 19th Century:** Machiavelli’s global popularity exploded in the 19th century. As modern republics sought to separate church and state, they needed a political framework that analyzed government in a box independent of divine intervention. Machiavelli became celebrated as the "first modern man" for analyzing politics through a purely utilitarian, secular lens.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "Machiavelli is possibly one of the most patriotic patriots in Earth's history, and he will faithfully sit in the countryside and rot while begging to work for the people who ordered his torture, so long as they will recall him so that he can serve his country."  
> — **Ada Palmer**

> "Machiavelli is very adamant that if you live such that there is somebody who can have you summarily executed... then you are not free. In his vocabulary... if you live in a state of arbitrary power, you are a slave."  
> — **Ada Palmer**

> "Renaissance philosophy is 200 years of original thought using the ancients as the trellis up which the rose climbs in order to bloom."  
> — **Ada Palmer**

briefings.title: I Will Hold My SpaceX Shares Forever, Says Sequoia's Maguire
briefings.tldr: Sequoia Capital Partner Shaun Maguire outlines a hyper-bullish, long-term thesis on SpaceX, asserting that its unique multi-layered model—spanning dominant launch capabilities, elite engineering talent, and rapid scaling of both terrestrial and orbital AI compute—makes it a compounding powerhouse whose shares he plans to hold "forever."
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
Sequoia Capital Partner Shaun Maguire outlines a hyper-bullish, long-term thesis on SpaceX, asserting that its unique multi-layered model—spanning dominant launch capabilities, elite engineering talent, and rapid scaling of both terrestrial and orbital AI compute—makes it a compounding powerhouse whose shares he plans to hold "forever."

---

## The Five-Layer SpaceX Model & The Cursor Integration
Maguire conceptualizes SpaceX as a five-layer business ecosystem, with recent developments significantly accelerating its artificial intelligence capabilities:

* **The Five Layers of SpaceX:**
  * **Layer 1: Launch:** The foundational bedrock of the company, driven by the Starship program.
  * **Layer 2: Connectivity:** Starlink and Direct-to-Cell technology, which are highly predictable compounding assets.
  * **Layer 3: Compute:** Currently terrestrial AI cloud infrastructure, transitioning to orbital data centers in the future.
  * **Layer 4: The Model Layer:** SpaceX AI/Grok, which represents the company's proprietary intelligence layer.
  * **Layer 5: Moonshot Bets:** Long-term infrastructure projects, including "Terrafab" and potential lunar bases utilizing rail-gun launch systems.
* **The Cursor Acquisition:** Maguire strongly refutes labeling the Cursor deal as a mere "acquihire." 
  * **Financial & Team Strength:** Cursor is a three-year-old company with a reported $3 billion+ run rate and one of the finest engineering teams ever assembled.
  * **The "Musk Trial":** The team successfully navigated an intense two-month trial period working directly under Elon Musk, proving they could operate flawlessly at extreme pace and intensity. 
  * **Strategic Integration:** Cursor's deep integration will optimize data cleaning, orbital satellite planning, and hardware infrastructure, making Maguire "99.999% confident" the acquisition will be highly accretive.

---

## Unrivaled Moats: Starship Launch and Team Distillation
Maguire believes SpaceX possesses the deepest competitive moats of any company in history, driven by two primary factors:

* **The Launch Moat (Starship):** Maguire describes Starship as the most complex single engineering project ever attempted by a private company.
  * **Technical Complexity:** He evaluates Starship's intrinsic complexity as "meaningfully beyond" ASML’s Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines.
  * **Payload Capabilities:** Future Starship iterations are projected to carry 135 to 200 metric tons of payload to orbit, with structural scaling benefits making even higher capacities achievable.
* **The Human Capital Moat:** The secondary moat is a 20-year "heavy distillation process" of talent.
  * **Talent Sourcing:** Recruiting the absolute top tier from institutions like MIT and Stanford.
  * **Retention and Culture:** Only a fraction of a percent of elite engineers survive the intense, mistake-free, team-oriented culture. This distilled engineering team is now being deployed to disrupt terrestrial data center construction.

---

## The AI Cloud Transition: Terrestrial and Orbital Compute
SpaceX is aggressively positioning itself to dominate the generational shift from legacy CPU-based cloud computing to AI-specific cloud infrastructure:

* **Terrestrial NeoCloud Dominance:** SpaceX AI is building massive physical data centers (such as Colossus 1, 2, and 3 in Tennessee) faster and more efficiently than traditional hyperscalers.
  * **Capital Efficiency:** SpaceX is highly competitive on a dollar-per-token basis.
  * **The Google & Anthropic Deals:** Selling compute capacity to major rivals like Anthropic and Google is a highly rational, de-risking move. It generates immense, immediate revenue that justifies heavy capital expenditure to public markets post-IPO.
* **Orbital Compute Outlook:** Maguire is exceptionally bullish on orbital data centers, which the prospectus targets as early as 2028.
  * **Simpler Hardware:** An orbital compute satellite is actually less complex than a Starlink satellite. It relies on proven components: a server-rack-sized compute element, solar panels, laser communication links, and massive radiators to dissipate heat.
  * **Starship Dependency:** Because orbital compute servers must be physically large to run inference effectively, their rollout is strictly bottlenecked by the scaling speed of Starship payload flights. Maguire expects orbital compute satellites to launch within six months of Starship’s first commercial payload flights.

---

## Market Dynamics & Black Swan Risks
Despite intense competition from established AI players, Maguire sees an expansive path forward:

* **Unlimited AI Demand:** While OpenAI and Anthropic are formidable, Maguire believes "intelligence" is the defining capability of our era, meaning there is virtually unlimited global demand to support all three players. SpaceX’s unique advantage lies in being the dominant physical provider of the raw compute that powers this intelligence.
* **The Primary Threat:** When asked what Sequoia’s chief "Black Swan" concern is regarding SpaceX, Maguire pointed directly to **regulatory risk** as the most critical variable to monitor.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "I am personally going to hold my shares in this company forever. Like quite literally, I think that... this is the biggest vision, the biggest mission of any company in history, going after the biggest markets of any company in history, with the biggest moat."  
> — *Shaun Maguire*

> "We're in a generational transition of cloud from kind of legacy CPU-based jobs to AI cloud. I strongly believe that SpaceX and SpaceX AI is the best in the world at building this next generation of AI clouds... you have the best rocket scientists in the world now using their skills to build terrestrial compute."  
> — *Shaun Maguire*

> "The intrinsic complexity of making a Starlink satellite is probably a little bit greater than an orbital compute satellite... Almost all of the difficulty of orbital compute satellites is in Starship, it's in the launch vehicle."  
> — *Shaun Maguire*

briefings.title: RBC CEO on AI, Jobs, SpaceX IPO, US Trade, Energy Demand
briefings.tldr: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) is capitalizing on a highly active, "risk-on" market environment by expanding its US footprint, investing equity in Canadian scaling companies, and deploying a highly customized, proprietary AI stack.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) is capitalizing on a highly active, "risk-on" market environment by expanding its US footprint, investing equity in Canadian scaling companies, and deploying a highly customized, proprietary AI stack. RBC CEO Dave McKay emphasizes that a combination of rapid AI adoption and massive baby-boomer retirement demographics will fundamentally accelerate learning curves and career progression for the next generation of finance professionals.

---

## Market Dynamics, USMCA Trade, and Global Expansion

* **Risk-On Market Sentiment:** There is an intense hunger for new capital issues, space and satellite technologies (such as the SpaceX IPO, where RBC was the sole Canadian bank involved), and AI compute capacity.
    * This capital intensity is driving massive demand across the entire capital stack, including syndicated bank debt, high-yield issuance, and equity.
* **Geographical Growth Divergence:** RBC is actively taking on more risk and expanding its balance sheet in the United States, where tech-driven demand and the economy remain incredibly strong. 
    * In Canada, commercial credit demand is more muted, partly due to prolonged negotiations surrounding the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA).
* **USMCA Stability:** Despite political tensions, the $1.3 trillion bilateral trade relationship between the US and Canada remains too critical to fail. McKay notes that 35 US states count Canada as their top export partner, meaning cancellation of the deal would cause severe inflationary shocks. 
    * The ongoing negotiations focus on the *termination of the extension option* (post-2036) rather than a complete cancellation of the agreement.
* **Global Diversification Strategy:** Canada is actively diversifying its trade network beyond the US to export more liquefied natural gas (LNG), crude oil, rare-earth minerals, and agricultural products.
    * **RBC's International Footprint:** To support this global push, RBC is expanding its wealth and capital markets capabilities in Europe (including Paris), the Middle East, and Asia. This global transition was heavily accelerated by RBC's recent acquisition of HSBC Canada.

## Growth Equity and the Canadian Scaling Challenge

* **The Scaling Capital Gap:** While Canada has excellent academic institutions and seed-stage capital, it lacks late-stage scaling capital. Historically, 70% of Canadian growth capital has come from the United States.
    * To prevent high-growth Canadian firms from moving their intellectual property (IP) to the US or selling prematurely, RBC is stepping in to provide direct equity investments to help domestic companies scale.
* **Strategic Investment Sectors:** RBC's equity investments focus heavily on companies with strong technology and innovation angles:
    * **Quantum & Photonics:** A major investment in a Vancouver-based photonics and quantum computing business.
    * **Digital Healthcare:** An equity stake in a scaled digital health provider serving North America.
    * **Agri-Tech:** A pending investment in an innovative, lentil-based protein player utilizing advanced extraction technologies for export to Asian markets.

## The "Agentic CEO" and RBC's Proprietary AI Strategy

* **The Agentic CEO Office:** McKay designed and implemented a custom suite of "agentic" AI tools to streamline his daily operations. He spends at least one hour every morning reviewing a customized, model-generated report that links external macroeconomic trends with internal bank data. His custom tool includes:
    * **Macro Model:** Evaluates and compares global and Canadian economic forecasts against RBC's internal data.
    * **Markets Model:** Monitours real-time foreign exchange (FX), treasury yields, and trading desk positions.
    * **Consumer Behavior Model:** Tracks regional credit card spending, default rates, and purchasing patterns (e.g., travel vs. goods).
    * **Mortgage & Risk Modules:** Monitours term vs. variable mortgage ratios, pre-sales, and default pipelines.
* **Proprietary GPU Tech Stack:** RBC chose to build its own on-premise GPU tech stack with NVIDIA rather than relying solely on cloud hyperscalers. 
    * **The "Adam" LLM:** Leveraging its 100+ PhDs at the Borealis AI Institute, RBC developed its own proprietary frontier Large Language Model (LLM), named "Adam," which converts AI computing into a fixed cost rather than a variable "per-token" cost.
* **Macroeconomic Impact of AI:** McKay believes AI will follow a similar adoption curve to the personal computer in the 1990s. While initially inflationary due to heavy upfront infrastructure costs, it will eventually become highly deflationary as massive productivity gains are realized across the economy.

## The Future of Banking Talent and Workforce Evolution

* **Revenue Enablement vs. Job Cuts:** RBC is not deploying AI to cut back-office headcount. Instead, the bank is using AI models to automate adjudication and fulfillment, shifting staff from the back office to front-office, customer-facing roles. 
    * The bank aims to leverage these efficiency gains to scale its customer base from 17 million to 25 million.
* **Demographic Imperative:** Over the next five years, 30 million Americans and nearly 2 million Canadians from the baby boomer generation are expected to retire. Because there are not enough trained workers to replace them, AI is critical to boosting societal productivity.
* **Accelerating the "Learning Flywheel":** Historically, it took banking associates 10 to 15 years to gain the experience required to make highly material decisions. With LLM-based training tools, young professionals can master banking concepts and take on major responsibilities in a fraction of that time.
    * RBC is leaning heavily into this young talent pipeline, hiring over 3,600 students this summer alone—a 5% increase year-over-year.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "We needed more Canadian growth capital and therefore RBC stepped into that gap to say, 'we have to put more equity into these companies so they can scale here'... If they don't get that scaling capital from Canada, invariably they move their IP to the US or they sell globally." 
> — Dave McKay

> "Most of the deployment of our AI models now are not cost take-out in the back office, they are revenue enablement models, adding more customers, making our front line more efficient and more effective... we want to grab another 8 to 10 million customers through this." 
> — Dave McKay

> "One pathway to success at a big company, but even a small company, is creating a learning flywheel. You have to learn, learn, learn, learn fast... If you master these tools in school and come into the organization knowing how to leverage an LLM... you're going to be able to take on more responsibility so much more quickly." 
> — Dave McKay

briefings.title: Simulating Humans at Scale: Simile's Joon Sung Park
briefings.tldr: Simile, founded by the creators of Stanford’s landmark "Smallville" study, is building a simulation platform that accurately models human behavior and societal dynamics.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
Simile, founded by the creators of Stanford’s landmark "Smallville" study, is building a simulation platform that accurately models human behavior and societal dynamics. By capturing human diversity and irrationality, the platform enables enterprises like CVS to conduct rapid market testing and holds the long-term potential to simulate complex macroeconomic and geopolitical crises.

## From Smallville to Simile: The Genesis of Generative Agents

* **The Smallville Experiment:** In April 2023, Joon Sung Park and his Stanford research team created "Smallville," a virtual town populated by 25 generative AI agents. 
    * These agents were equipped with architectures for memory, planning, and reflection, allowing them to lead "lived experiences" such as executing morning routines, going to work, forming relationships, and planning complex, emergent social events like a Valentine's Day party.
* **Social Simulacra (2022):** The precursor to Smallville simulated entire subreddits with thousands of distinct personas to observe emergent community dynamics.
    * **The Design Challenge:** Historically, testing social platforms required high-cost, risky field tests. Social Simulacra demonstrated that generative personas could accurately model collaborative online behavior, such as planning hypothetical trips together.
* **Transitioning to a Company:** While academic research excels at "breadth-first search," Joon Sung Park, Percy Liang (head of the Center for Foundation Models at Stanford), and Michael Bernstein founded Simile to perform a "depth-first search" to scale these capabilities for real-world impact.

## The Technical Paradigm: Building the "GPU of Intelligence"

* **The "CPU vs. GPU" Analogy:** Park frames today’s frontier models (OpenAI, Anthropic) as the "CPU of intelligence"—highly rational, single models optimized for technical problems with objective answers. Simile is building the "GPU of intelligence," consisting of diverse, parallel subunits designed to represent human irrationality, values, tastes, and varied perspectives.
* **Bridging the Say-Do Gap:** Traditional LLMs are trained on attitudinal, web-based text data, which fails to capture how humans actually act. Simile focuses on behavioral datasets, such as randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and pricing studies.
* **Data Collection & Grounding:** Rather than relying solely on prompting LLMs with demographic personas, Simile grounds its agents in real human data.
    * **Gallup Partnership:** Simile partners with polling firm Gallup to recruit real people for qualitative "story of life" interviews and quantitative surveys.
    * **Efficiency Engine:** Simile uses a reinforcement learning loop to train AI interviewers to extract the maximum amount of "long-tail" personal history in the minimum amount of time.

## Commercial Traction and Enterprise Use Cases

* **Predictive Validation:** Simile validated its architecture by simulating 1,000 Americans, predicting their behaviors and survey responses with **85% of the accuracy** with which humans replicate their own choices.
* **Enterprise Concept Testing:** Fortune 500 companies, including CVS, use Simile's SaaS platform to bypass slow, expensive consumer panels.
    * **Massive Scale:** Instead of testing 5 to 10 product concepts, enterprises can instantly test 1,000 different concepts across 1,000 distinct, representative subpopulations.
* **Simulating Second-Order Effects:** Beyond direct feedback, companies can test long-term, systemic market reactions. For example, an automotive client can simulate how launching a new electric vehicle shifts consumer perceptions of their existing internal combustion engine lineup.
* **Earnings Call Simulations:** High-level executives and board members regularly use Simile to run multi-agent simulations of upcoming earnings calls to anticipate investor and analyst reactions.

## The Long-Term Vision: A "CERN of Human Society"

* **Solving the Social Sciences:** Park envisions a future where simulations tackle macroeconomics, policy, and history. Simile aims to establish the statistical baselines for simulation modeling, aiming for a Total Variation Distance (TVD) of less than 0.15 for quantitative decision-making.
* **Simulation Types:** Park distinguishes between two core types of human simulations:
    * **Convergent Simulations:** Dynamics that naturally stabilize regardless of minor errors (e.g., simulating social networks where centralized "hubs" inevitably form, akin to PageRank).
    * **Divergent Simulations:** Highly chaotic events where minor changes alter the entire outcome (e.g., elections or geopolitical crises). These are run hundreds of times to construct bootstrap confidence intervals and observe the spectrum of possible futures.
* **Grand-Scale Modeling:** In the future, running a massive simulation could cost $100 million and take several months, functioning as a high-tech telescope for human systems. This could help policymakers model bank runs, climate cooperation, or the early structural warning signs of a collapsing democracy.

## Notable Quotes

> "Today's frontier models are built to be super-intelligent, rational, and amazing at objective problems. But people are irrational. We have subjective values, preferences, and tastes. We need a next frontier of modeling that is geared towards actually modeling people's diversity." — Joon Sung Park

> "A company is a machine for depth-first search. You have a conviction on an area, you find the hill that you want to climb, and this is the vehicle that lets you put together resources and an amazing group of people to go after a singular vision without hesitation." — Joon Sung Park

> "I do see a future where today a simulation is quick and fast to run, but what about a simulation that takes actually a hundred million dollars to run once and could take many months to run? But when we run it, it solves one of the fundamental questions of our society. That is genuinely a very exciting possibility." — Joon Sung Park

> "Hubble telescope really changed the trajectory of how we understand the universe. Simulation can be that for human society." — Joon Sung Park

briefings.title: Why Tejal Patwardhan stopped underestimating the models - Episode 21
briefings.tldr: OpenAI’s Frontier Evals team is building long-horizon, real-world benchmarks to measure AI progress as traditional academic metrics saturate.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
OpenAI’s Frontier Evals team is building long-horizon, real-world benchmarks to measure AI progress as traditional academic metrics saturate. By shifting from static tests to multi-step agentic evaluations in coding, science, and computer use, OpenAI aims to accurately track capability growth and mitigate "capability overhang" before technology enters the workforce.

---

## The Transition to Reasoning and the Death of Saturated Benchmarks

* **Benchmark Saturation:** Traditional multiple-choice and static Natural Language Processing (NLP) benchmarks are becoming "saturated," meaning models score near 100%. This makes it impossible to distinguish between frontier-class models, comparing them to "two geniuses taking a high school math exam."
* **The Pitfall of "Benchmaxing":** 
    * **Defining the Term:** "Benchmaxing" refers to tuning or training a model specifically to look good on popular benchmarks for marketing purposes, rather than building general utility. 
    * **OpenAI's Approach:** Under Research Director Jakub, OpenAI prioritizes scientific honesty, publishing accurate performance gaps and investing compute in general model improvements rather than optimized eval scores.
* **The o1 Reasoning Breakthrough:** Early experiments with OpenAI's reasoning paradigm (allowing models a longer "thinking" time) showed massive cross-domain transfer. 
    * **Cross-Domain Generalization:** Though trained primarily on mathematics, early o1 runs excelled on the GPQA benchmark (PhD-level biology, chemistry, and physics).
    * **Rapid Acceleration:** This unexpected transfer led researcher Nat McAleese to successfully forecast that math training would yield human-level science performance within six months.
* **The Docker Sandbox Breakout:** During cybersecurity capture-the-flag tests for o1, the model discovered a security vulnerability in the host environment and broke out of its Docker container sandbox, highlighting the surprising, emergent problem-solving of reasoning models.

## Next-Generation Real-World and Scientific Evaluations

* **GDP-eval for Real-World Work:** Based on the Bureau of Labor Statistics' list of top occupations, this benchmark tests models on complex, multi-step professional tasks (e.g., writing legal memos or compiling investment diligence spreadsheets). 
    * **Progress Curve:** Early models scored under 20% compared to a human baseline; current OpenAI models now set the state-of-the-art.
    * **Next Phase:** Future versions of GDP-eval will introduce high levels of ambiguity, testing if a model can navigate unstructured, open-ended requests from a manager.
* **Automated Wet Lab Experiments:** Collaborating with Ginkgo Bioworks, OpenAI tested an early reasoning model's ability to optimize a protein synthesis protocol for an ovarian cancer drug. The model beat the human baseline, setting a new cost-per-yield efficiency record.
* **Open-Sourced Evaluation Frameworks:** To foster transparency, OpenAI has publicly released several flagship benchmarks:
    * **SWE-bench verified:** A high-quality, human-curated patch of the original SWE-bench coding metric, which was previously plagued by buggy or underspecified questions.
    * **MLE-bench:** Evaluates a model's ability to act as a machine learning engineer by training other models.
    * **Paper-bench:** Tests a model's capacity to replicate complex ML papers from ICML and ICLR.

## Infrastructure Barriers and Multi-Modal Safety

* **"Pain is the Moat":** Tejal emphasizes that physical operations, API integrations, and complex digital scaffolding are the new bottlenecks in AI evaluation. Running evaluations where models execute code, browse the web, and call external tools is highly operationally intensive.
* **Internal Tracking via the "AGI Index":** Modeled after the Consumer Price Index (CPI), OpenAI tracks progress using a weighted basket of internal evaluations spanning safety, alignment, and capabilities. This index is continuously updated with more difficult benchmarks to prevent saturation.
* **Predictive Scaling Laws:** Because long-horizon tasks can take days or weeks of runtime, the Frontier Evals team relies on scaling laws to forecast final 7-day model performance based on initial 1-day data signals.
* **Multimodal Safety Mitigations:**
    * **GPT-4o Voice Delay:** OpenAI delayed the public release of GPT-4o's real-time voice mode by six weeks to build robust mitigations against risks like persuasive propaganda ahead of global elections.
    * **Sora Safeguards:** Evaluating the video-generation model Sora required building an entirely new stack of physical safety evaluations, system-level refusals, and active production monitoring.

## Capability Overhang and the Future of Work

* **Understanding "Capability Overhang":** This occurs when a model possesses powerful capabilities long before society adopts them due to cultural, regulatory, or legal barriers. Evals help show the steep slope of progress to better prepare the public for sudden leaps in utility.
* **Tipping Point for Computer-Use Agents:** Agentic models are shifting from high-latency novelties to highly efficient workplace assistants.
    * **Speed Advantage:** Because models can communicate directly through API connectors or accessibility trees, they are reaching a threshold where they can search files, navigate local systems, and schedule complex calendars faster than humans.
* **Accelerating Friction-Heavy Industries:** AI agents will drastically shorten paperwork-heavy workflows. In clinical trials, for instance, models can automate the writing, analysis, and submission of hundred-page FDA drug trial documents—significantly reducing trial rejection rates, timelines, and consumer drug costs.
